column4: We, His followers, are to *“go and make disciples of all nations.”* Discipleship is about personal growth and about multiplying that growth by teaching others to follow Christ. Discipleship is the vehicle through which we build the Kingdom of God; the teachings of Jesus are the message.
column5: We, His followers, are to *“Go and make disciples of all nations.”* Discipleship is personal growth as well as teaching others to follow Christ in order to multiply that growth. Discipleship is the means by which we build God's kingdom; Jesus' teachings are the message.

column4: The call to be a disciple is more than attending church or learning Bible verses-it is an invitation to live like Jesus and to partner with Him in advancing God’s Kingdom. Genuine discipleship helps believers become spiritually mature and effective for ministry (Ephesians 4:13). It shapes both the heart and skills needed to serve others and share the Gospel. As Paul instructed Timothy in 2 Timothy 2:2, discipleship follows a pattern of spiritual multiplication, where trained disciples continue raising up new followers to lead other to Christ.
column5: The call to be a disciple is more than merely attending church or learning Bible verses—it is an invitation to live like Jesus and, together with Him, advance God's kingdom. True discipleship makes believers spiritually mature and effective for ministry (Ephesians 4:13). It shapes both the heart and the skills that are necessary to serve others and share the gospel. As Paul instructed Timothy in 2 Timothy 2:2, discipleship follows a pattern of spiritual multiplication, where trained disciples keep raising up new followers to bring others to Christ.

column4: Discipleship is both an individual calling and a global mission. On a personal level, it involves growing in faith, developing an active spiritual life, being in relationship with others & God. At the same time, it fuels the mission of the Church to reach every nation with the Gospel, ensuring that the message of Christ continues to expand and transform lives across generations.
column5: Discipleship is both an individual calling and a global mission. On a personal level, it involves growing in faith, cultivating a vibrant spiritual life, being in relationship with others & with God. At the same time, it fuels the church's mission to bring the gospel to every nation, so that the message of Christ continues to spread from generation to generation and transform lives.

column4: The impact of discipleship goes beyond personal transformation-it has a Kingdom impact. Paul reminded Timothy in 2 Timothy 2:2 to entrust what He had learned to faithful men who would then teach others also. This generational pattern highlights how discipleship is the engine that drives the growth and sustainability of the Church. Discipleship matters because it was Jesus’ chosen method for spreading the Gospel and building His Church.

column4: Rather than focusing on large crowds, Jesus intentionally invested in a small group of followers, teaching them, modeling faithfulness, and preparing them to carry forward His mission. column4: At its core, discipleship is central to fulfilling the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20). Jesus did not just call us to make converts but to make disciples-followers who are grounded in God’s Word, empowered by the Holy Spirit, and equipped for ministry. Through discipleship, believers grow in their knowledge of Scripture, develop spiritual disciplines, and learn to walk in obedience to Christ. It prepares the Church to impact the world, advance the Gospel, and reflect the glory of God to all nations.

Through discipleship, believers grow in knowledge of Scripture, develop spiritual habits, and learn to walk in obedience to Christ. It prepares the church to influence the world, advance the gospel, and display a glimpse of God's glory to all nations.

column4: ### Nature vs Nurture
column5: ### Nature vs. Nurture

column4: In the study of biology, psychology, and anthropology we often consider the impact of nature versus nurture. The question often posed, is a person more the result of their innate, in-built genetic heritage? Or are they more the result of their environment and upbringing? The truth is that every person is a blend of nature and nurture. Both elements in strong interplay choreograph the development of a human soul.
column5: In the study of biology, psychology, and anthropology we often consider the effects of nature versus nurture. The question is often: Is a person more the result of his or her inborn, inherent genetic heritage? Or are they more the result of their environment and upbringing? The truth is that every person is a combination of nature and nurture. The strong interplay of both elements shapes the development of the human soul.

column4: When you accepted Jesus, the miracle of salvation made you born-again of incorruptible seed. You received a godly nature! Your spiritual DNA was re-written! This godly nature causes a stirring in our hearts to be close to our heavenly Father, to know Him, to experience Him.
column5: When you accepted Jesus, the miracle of salvation caused you to be born again of incorruptible seed. You received the divine nature! Your spiritual DNA was rewritten! This divine nature stirs our hearts to be close to our heavenly Father, to know Him, to experience Him.

column4: Just as a new-born, whose wonderful, beautiful, innocent nature must be shaped by loving parents to develop into a healthy and mature individual, we too must be shaped and nurtured to be developed.
column5: Like a newborn whose marvelous, beautiful, innocent nature must be shaped by the nurture of loving parents in order to become a healthy and mature person, so we too must be shaped and nurtured in order for us to grow.

column4: Discipleship is the process of spiritual development that builds upon our godly nature and makes us spiritually mature. Through investing in discipleship, we ensure that faith is passed down, leaders are raised up, and the Church remains healthy and vibrant-both locally and globally.
column5: Discipleship is the process of spiritual growth that builds upon our divine nature and matures us spiritually. Through investment in discipleship we ensure that the faith is passed on, leaders are raised up, and the church remains healthy and vibrant—both locally and globally.

column4: ### Didactic Model vs Apprentice Model
column5: ### Didactic Model vs. Discipleship/Apprenticeship Model

column4: In modern day western education, the primary relationship the student has is with the material. The student’s learning is focused on content, material, books, videos, assignments, etc. The transformation of education happens via the curriculum. This method of teaching is known as the *didactic model*.
column5: In modern Western education, the student's primary engagement is with the content. The student's learning centers on content, books, videos, assignments, etc. Transformation in education occurs through the curriculum. This approach to teaching is called the *didactic model*.

column4: The paradigm of the didactic model has not always been the norm. The model and method used in Jesus’ age was the *apprentice model.* This model of learning emphasizes knowledge being more ‘caught than taught’ and focuses more on the relationship between student and teacher, than student and curriculum.
column5: The paradigm of the classroom model has not always been the norm. In Jesus' time, the model and method used was the *discipleship model*. This model of learning emphasizes that knowledge is more often 'caught' than taught and focuses more on the relationship between student and teacher than on the student and the curriculum.

column4: The didactic model gradually became the default method over about a millennium, from the first medieval universities of Europe in the 11<sup>th</sup> - 13<sup>th</sup> centuries, the invention of the printing press in the 15<sup>th</sup> century, the enlightenment of the 17<sup>th</sup> & 18<sup>th</sup> century, and the impact of industrial revolution on information and education in the 19<sup>th</sup> & 20<sup>th</sup> centuries.
column5: The classroom model gradually became the standard method over roughly a thousand years: the early medieval universities of Europe (11<sup>th</sup> - 13<sup>th</sup> centuries), the invention of the printing press in the 15<sup>th</sup> century, the Enlightenment of the 17<sup>th</sup> & 18<sup>th</sup> centuries, and the effects of the Industrial Revolution on information and education in the 19<sup>th</sup> & 20<sup>th</sup> centuries.

column4: The advantage of the didactic model is that it can scale more efficiently than the apprentice model. Massively open online courses (MOOCs) can have thousands of students at the same time, whereas even a very skilled master can only have perhaps a few dozen apprentices concurrently.
column5: The advantage of the classroom model is that it can scale more effectively than the discipleship model. Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) can accommodate thousands of students at once, whereas even a very skilled teacher may be able to have only a few dozen disciples at a time.

column4: The result of the didactic model is that the student has mastery of content, however the student does not become like the teacher. The teacher is a facilitator for the curriculum. The teacher imparts knowledge.
column5: The outcome of the classroom model is that the student masters the material; however, the student does not become like the teacher. The teacher is a facilitator for the curriculum. The teacher transfers knowledge.

column4: In the apprentice model the master shares more than knowledge, he imparts wisdom. The result of the apprentice model is that the student has become like the master so completely that the student can reproduce the work of the master and take on apprentices of his own.
column5: In the discipleship model the teacher shares not only knowledge, but also imparts wisdom. The result of the discipleship model is that the disciple becomes so like the teacher that they can replicate the teacher's work and make their own disciples.

column4: The didactic model has its use and place in the Kingdom of God, a good example is this book or any other Christian educational material. Jesus as a rabbi, skilled and trained in the rabbinical method, practiced the apprentice model as the primary model for His disciples.
column5: The classroom model has its place and usefulness in God's Kingdom; a good example is this book or any Christian educational material. Jesus, as a rabbi who was skilled and trained in the rabbinic way, primarily adopted the discipleship model for his disciples.

column4: ## Jesus’ Model and Process of Discipleship
column5: ## Jesus' model and method for discipleship

column4: Jesus demonstrated the mature and complete example of discipleship in the Gospels with His chosen disciples. We should use these steps broadly as the foundation for our own walk in becoming and making disciples.
column5: In the Gospels, Jesus presented a robust and complete example of discipleship with his chosen disciples. We should broadly adopt these stages as a foundation for becoming and making disciples in our lives.

column4: The apprentice model has two roles: master and student. Every master has been a student, and hopefully every student will become a master. I will use the terms *disciple* to refer to the student and *disciple-maker* to refer to the master/teacher.
column5: In the discipleship model there are two roles: teacher and student. Every teacher was once a student, and hopefully every student will become a teacher. I will use the term *disciple* for the student, and *disciple-maker* for the teacher/instructor.

column4: Every discipleship relationship goes through a progression of eight phases. In each phase there is an emphasis for the disciple, and for the disciple-maker. We will study attributes of disciple-makers in depth later in this chapter.

In each stage there is a particular emphasis for the disciple and for the disciple-maker. Later in this chapter we will study the qualities of disciple-makers in detail.

column4: ### Invitation/Calling
column5: ### Invitation/Call

column4: Discipleship begins with a personal invitation from Jesus to follow Him. In Matthew 4:19, Jesus called His first disciples, saying, *“Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.”* This invitation was both relational and transformational-it required leaving behind old ways of life and stepping into a new purpose centered on God’s mission. Jesus’ call wasn’t to spectatorship but to participation in His ministry and Kingdom work.
column5: Discipleship begins with a personal invitation from Jesus to follow Him. In Matthew 4:19 Jesus called His first disciples, saying: *"Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men."* This invitation was both relational and transformative-it required leaving the old way of life behind and stepping into a new purpose centered on God’s mission. Jesus’s call was not toward becoming spectators but toward participation in His ministry and the work of the Kingdom.

column4: Modern disciple-makers must invite others into authentic relationships that inspire spiritual growth and obedience. The invitation to discipleship is deeply personal. Jesus meets individuals where they are, addressing their unique needs and circumstances, but He also calls them to go deeper-to grow, serve, and become more like Him. This pattern reflects the relational nature of discipleship, where the focus is not merely on knowledge but on a life-changing relationship with Christ.
column5: Those who make disciples today should invite others into genuine relationships that spur spiritual growth and obedience. The call to discipleship is profoundly personal. Jesus meets individuals where they are, addressing their unique needs and circumstances, yet He also calls them to go deeper-grow, serve, and become like Him. This pattern reveals the relational nature of discipleship, where the focus is not merely on knowledge but on a life-transforming relationship with Christ.

column4: ### Teaching
column5: ### Teaching

column4: Teaching is at the heart of discipleship. Jesus spent much of His ministry teaching the principles of the Kingdom of God, most notably in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7). His teachings provided a foundation for living righteously, loving others, and walking in obedience to God. Instruction in the Word of God remains central to discipleship today, as Scripture is the primary tool for spiritual growth, correction, and training in righteousness (2 Timothy 3:16-17).
column5: Teaching is at the heart of discipleship. Jesus devoted much of His ministry to teaching the principles of God’s Kingdom, especially in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7). His teachings provided the foundation for living righteously, loving others, and walking in obedience to God. Even today, instruction in the Scriptures is central to discipleship, because the Bible is the primary instrument for spiritual growth, reproof, and training in righteousness (2 Timothy 3:16-17).

column4: Disciple-makers must commit to teaching the Bible faithfully, helping others understand and apply it to their lives. Teaching involves more than imparting knowledge-it requires modeling Christ-like living so disciples can see faith in action. Jesus embodied the truths He taught, showing that effective teaching is both verbal and visible. In the same way, disciple-makers should strive to live out what they teach, providing practical examples of obedience and faithfulness.
column5: Disciple-makers should teach the Bible faithfully, helping others understand it and apply it to their lives. Teaching is not merely the transfer of information-it also requires modeling a Christlike life so that disciples can see the faith in action. Jesus embodied the truths He taught, showing that effective teaching is both spoken and visible. Likewise, disciple-makers should live what they teach, providing practical examples of obedience and faithfulness.

column4: ### Demonstrating
column5: ### Practical Demonstration

column4: Jesus didn’t just teach His disciples- He demonstrated how to live out the truths He proclaimed. Jesus showed what it means to love, serve, and minister in practical ways. Some examples from the gospels are Jesus washing the disciples’ feet as an act of humility and service (John 13:12-15), healing the sick, and feeding the hungry. Through His actions, He modeled compassion, faith, and boldness, leaving a clear example for His followers to imitate.
column5: Jesus did not merely teach His disciples- He also showed them how to live out the truths He proclaimed. Jesus demonstrated what it means to love, serve, and minister in practical ways. Here are a few examples from the Gospels: Jesus washed the disciples’ feet as an act of humility and service (John 13:12-15), healed the sick, and fed the hungry. Through His actions He modeled compassion, faith, and courage, leaving a clear example for His followers to imitate.

column4: Discipleship requires showing, not just telling. Modern disciple-makers must be transparent about their faith journey, including struggles and victories, so others can see how faith works in real life. Whether it’s praying with someone in need, sharing testimonies, or serving the community, discipleship thrives when it’s rooted in practical demonstration. Actions often speak louder than words, making demonstration a powerful tool for training others in the faith.
column5: Discipleship requires not only telling but also showing. Today’s disciple-makers should be transparent about their faith journeys, including both struggles and victories, so that others can see how faith works in real life. Whether praying with someone in need, sharing testimonies, or serving the community, discipleship thrives when it is rooted in practical demonstration. Actions often speak louder than words, making demonstration a powerful means of training others in the faith.

column4: ### Participation/Trying
column5: ### Involvement/Effort

column4: Jesus didn’t keep His disciples on the sidelines- He actively involved them in ministry experiences. In Luke 9:1-6 and Matthew 10:5-15, Jesus sent the disciples out to preach the Gospel, heal the sick, and cast out demons. These hands-on opportunities allowed the disciples to learn by doing, gaining confidence and skills under His guidance.
column5: Jesus did not keep His disciples on the sidelines- He actively involved them in ministry experiences. In Luke 9:1-6 and Matthew 10:5-15, Jesus sent the disciples out to proclaim the gospel, heal the sick, and cast out demons. These hands-on opportunities allowed the disciples to learn by doing, so that they would gain confidence and skill under His guidance.

column4: Modern discipleship should also include practical involvement. Disciple-makers must invite disciples to participate in ministry, whether through leading prayer groups, sharing testimonies, or serving in outreach events. Providing safe spaces for practice allows disciples to grow in boldness while being supported and encouraged. Learning happens best when it is applied, and participation is the key to turning theory into action.
column5: Modern discipleship should also include practical involvement. Disciple makers should invite disciples to participate in service, whether through leading prayer groups, sharing testimonies, or serving at outreach events. Providing safe spaces for practice gives disciples the opportunity to grow in courage while they also receive support and encouragement. Learning is best when it is put into practice, and involvement is the key that turns theory into action.

column4: ### Correction
column5: ### Correction

column4: Growth often requires correction, and Jesus lovingly corrected His disciples when they misunderstood His teachings or failed in their tasks. In Mark 9:33-37, He addressed their pride by teaching them about servant leadership. In Luke 22:31-32, He prayed for Peter, preparing Him to recover from failure and strengthen others.
column5: Growth often requires correction, and Jesus lovingly corrected his disciples when they misunderstood his teachings or failed in their actions. In Mark 9:33-37, he addressed their pride by teaching about servant leadership. In Luke 22:31-32, he prayed for Peter, preparing him to recover from failure and strengthen others.

column4: Correction in discipleship should be grace-filled and constructive-rooted in Scripture and aimed at restoration (2 Timothy 4:2). It is not about condemnation but about helping disciples grow and avoid pitfalls. Disciple-makers should provide accountability, using God’s Word to guide and encourage growth while modeling humility in receiving correction themselves.
column5: Correction in discipleship should be grace-filled and constructive—rooted in Scripture and focused on restoration (2 Timothy 4:2). It is not about condemnation but about helping disciples grow and avoid pitfalls. Disciple makers should provide accountability, using God’s Word to guide and encourage growth, while modeling humility in receiving correction themselves.

column4: ### Empowerment/Authorization
column5: ### Empowerment/Authorization

column4: Jesus didn’t just teach and correct- He empowered His disciples to carry out His mission. He gave them authority to preach the Gospel, heal the sick, and cast out demons (Matthew 28:18-20). After His resurrection, He promised the Holy Spirit as the source of power for their ministry (Acts 1:8).
column5: Jesus not only taught and corrected—he empowered his disciples to carry out his mission. He gave them authority to preach the gospel, heal the sick, and cast out demons (Matthew 28:18-20). After his resurrection, he promised the Holy Spirit as the source of power for their ministry (Acts 1:8).

column4: Modern discipleship should include empowering others to operate in their spiritual gifts and minister effectively. This involves identifying gifts (Ephesians 4:11-13), encouraging their use, and releasing disciples to serve. Empowerment also emphasizes reliance on the Holy Spirit for strength, boldness, and wisdom, ensuring disciples are spiritually equipped for the work God has called them to do.
column5: Modern discipleship should include empowering others to operate in their spiritual gifts and minister effectively. This includes identifying gifts (Ephesians 4:11-13), encouraging their use, and sending disciples out for service. Empowerment also emphasizes reliance on the Holy Spirit for power, boldness, and wisdom, so that disciples are spiritually equipped for the work God has called them to.

column4: ### Multiplication
column5: ### Multiplication

column4: The goal of discipleship isn’t just personal growth-it’s multiplication. Jesus modeled this by training the disciples to make more disciples (Matthew 28:19-20). After His resurrection, the apostles continued this multiplying mission, spreading the Gospel and planting churches across the known world. Paul’s instructions in 2 Timothy 2:2 reinforce this principle, urging Timothy to teach others who will teach others.
column5: The goal of discipleship is not merely personal growth—it is multiplication. Jesus modeled this by training disciples who would make more disciples (Matthew 28:19-20). After his resurrection, the apostles continued this expanding mission, spreading the gospel and planting churches throughout the known world of their time. Paul’s instructions in 2 Timothy 2:2 reinforce this principle, urging Timothy to teach others who will in turn teach others.

column4: Discipleship involves equipping disciples to disciple others, creating a chain reaction of faith that expands the Kingdom of God. This process requires intentionality-teaching disciples how to mentor, teach, and train others, while sending them out with confidence and purpose (Romans 10:15).
column5: Discipleship involves equipping disciples to disciple others, creating a chain reaction of faith that advances God’s kingdom. This process requires intentionality—teaching disciples how to guide, teach, and train others, while also sending them with confidence and purpose (Romans 10:15).

column4: ### Remain Connected
column5: ### Maintain Contact

column4: Discipleship doesn’t end when someone is sent out. Jesus modeled ongoing connection with His disciples, continuing to encourage and instruct them even after His resurrection (John 21:15-19). The early church maintained this pattern, gathering regularly for teaching, fellowship, and prayer (Acts 2:42-47).
column5: Discipleship does not end when someone is sent. Jesus modeled ongoing contact with his disciples, continuing to encourage and instruct them even after his resurrection (John 21:15-19). The early church maintained the same pattern, gathering regularly for teaching, fellowship, and prayer (Acts 2:42-47).

column4: Modern discipleship should also foster ongoing relationships, providing accountability, encouragement, and support as disciples continue to grow and lead. Maintaining unity in the Body of Christ ensures that disciples are never isolated but remain strengthened and encouraged in their faith journey.
column5: Modern discipleship should also cultivate ongoing relationships, providing accountability, encouragement, and support as disciples continue to grow and lead. Maintaining unity in the body of Christ ensures that disciples are never alone but remain strengthened and encouraged in their journey of faith.

column4: ## Who does Discipleship?
column5: ## Who Does Discipleship?

column4: Everyone in the body of Christ is responsible first to become a disciple, then to contribute to the process of discipleship making. There are diversities of gifts and functions, so our contributions may look different, but we are all responsible. The people ultimately most responsible for the state and health of discipleship in the local church are the leaders (**elders and deacons - Acts 14:23**), but everyone plays a part.
column5: Everyone in the body of Christ bears the responsibility first to be a disciple, then to participate in making disciples. There is diversity in gifts and roles, so our contributions may look different, but we are all responsible. In the local church, the people ultimately most responsible for the state and health of discipleship are the leaders (**elders and deacons - Acts 14:23**), but everyone plays their part.

column4: Discipleship is a living, growing process-like nurturing a child to maturity. Healthy discipleship brings strength and life to people. Like a parent who strengthens and nourishes a child, and in doing so causes them to be healthy and mature, disciple-makers to help nourish, strengthen, and mature disciples. The end goal of discipleship is not ‘knowledge transfer’, but transformation.
column5: Discipleship is a living, growing process—like nurturing a child to maturity. Healthy discipleship empowers and gives life to people. Just as a parent strengthens and feeds a child, thereby making them healthy and mature, so disciple makers help to feed, strengthen, and mature disciples. The ultimate goal of discipleship is not 'transfer of knowledge,' but transformation.

column4: All of us must become perfect (mature) and make disciples. While we will have diverse gifts there are common characteristics for all disciple-makers.
column5: We are all to become perfect (mature) and make disciples. Although our gifts will differ, there are certain common characteristics for all disciple makers.

column4: ### Characteristics of a Disciple-Maker
column5: ### Characteristics of a Disciple Maker

column4: A disciple-maker is someone who not only follows Christ but is also committed to helping others grow in their faith. This role requires specific characteristics that reflect both spiritual maturity and practical dedication. Disciple-makers must continually rely on God’s strength, wisdom, and grace to overcome the challenges that come with leading others in their spiritual journeys.
column5: A disciple maker is someone who not only follows Christ but remains committed to helping others grow in their faith. This role requires specific qualities that reflect both spiritual maturity and practical dedication. Disciple makers should continually rely on God’s power, wisdom, and grace to overcome the challenges that come with guiding others in their spiritual journey.

column4: #### Rooted in Christ
column5: #### Rooted in Christ

column4: The foundation of a disciple-maker’s life must be deeply rooted in Christ. Jesus said, *“I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing”* (John 15:5). Effective disciple-makers know that the ability to grow and help others comes from staying close to Jesus every day. However, resistance to personal growth and spiritual change can hinder this dependence. Disciple-makers must continually cultivate their personal relationship with Jesus through prayer, study of Scripture, and obedience, modeling what it means to abide in Christ for those they are discipling.
column5: The foundation of a disciple-maker’s life should be deeply rooted in Christ. Jesus said، *“I am the vine؛ you are the branches. If you remain in Me and I in you، you will bear much fruit؛ apart from Me you can do nothing”* (John 15:5)۔ Effective disciple-makers know that the ability to grow and to help others comes from staying close to Jesus daily۔ However، personal growth and resistance to spiritual transformation can hinder this dependence۔ Disciple-makers should continually cultivate their personal relationship with Jesus through prayer، study of Scripture، and obedience, and model practically for those they are training what it means to abide in Christ۔

column4: #### Committed to the Mission
column5: #### Committed to the Mission

column4: A disciple-maker must remain committed to the mission of making disciples as commanded by Jesus in the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20). This mission requires intentional focus and prioritization, recognizing that disciple-making is not an optional task but the core purpose of the church. Yet, challenges such as time constraints, busyness, and personal distractions can make it difficult to stay focused. Disciple-makers must intentionally schedule time for mentoring, teaching, and relationship-building, viewing disciple-making as a lifestyle rather than an occasional activity (Luke 19:10).
column5: A disciple-maker should remain committed to the mission of making disciples as Jesus commanded in the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20)۔ This mission requires intentional focus and prioritization، knowing that making disciples is not an optional task but the church’s primary purpose۔ Even so، challenges such as lack of time، busyness، and personal distractions can make it difficult to stay focused۔ Disciple-makers should intentionally set aside time for mentoring، teaching، and building relationships, and view disciple-making not as an occasional activity but as a lifestyle (Luke 19:10)۔

column4: #### Spirit-Led
column5: #### Led by the Spirit

column4: Disciple-making cannot be accomplished in human strength alone; it requires the guidance and empowerment of the Holy Spirit. Jesus promised His disciples that they would receive power when the Holy Spirit came upon them (Acts 1:8), equipping them to be witnesses and ministers of the Gospel. Disciple-makers must be sensitive to the Spirit’s leading, relying on His wisdom to navigate complex situations, cultural barriers, and difficult conversations. This reliance on the Holy Spirit enables disciple-makers to operate in love, boldness, and spiritual discernment, ensuring their efforts are Spirit-directed rather than self-directed.
column5: Disciple-making cannot be done by human strength alone؛ it requires the guidance and power of the Holy Spirit۔ Jesus promised His disciples that when the Holy Spirit came upon them they would receive power (Acts 1:8)، and they would be equipped to be witnesses and servants of the gospel۔ Disciple-makers should remain sensitive to the Spirit’s leading، and rely on His wisdom to navigate complex situations، cultural barriers، and difficult conversations۔ This dependence on the Holy Spirit enables disciple-makers to act with love، courage، and spiritual discernment, so that their efforts are Spirit-directed rather than self-directed۔

column4: #### Humble and Teachable
column5: #### Humble and Teachable

column4: Humility is a hallmark of an effective disciple-maker. As Paul instructed, *“Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves”* (Philippians 2:3). Disciple-makers recognize that they, too, are lifelong learners who must remain teachable and accountable. They invite correction and feedback, modeling humility for those they mentor. Pride can be a significant barrier to growth, both for disciple-makers and their disciples. Embracing accountability and maintaining a servant’s heart fosters trust and creates an environment for growth and transparency.
column5: Humility is a distinguishing mark of an effective disciple-maker۔ As Paul instructed، *“Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves”* (Philippians 2:3)۔ Disciple-makers acknowledge that they themselves are lifelong learners who must remain teachable and accountable۔ They welcome correction and feedback، and model humility for those they train۔ Pride، can be a major barrier to growth، whether for disciple-makers or for their disciples۔ Embracing accountability and maintaining a servant’s heart fosters trust and creates an environment for growth and transparency۔

column4: #### Patient and Persistent
column5: #### Patient and Steadfast

column4: Discipleship is rarely instantaneous-it is a long-term process that requires patience and persistence. Paul reminds believers to *“not grow weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up”* (Galatians 6:9). Growth in faith often involves setbacks, questions, and failures, but disciple-makers are called to walk alongside others, offering encouragement and support through every step. It is easy to become discouraged when progress seems slow, but disciple-makers trust that God is at work, even when results are not immediately visible.
column5: Discipleship is rarely immediate-it is a long-term process that requires patience and perseverance۔ Paul reminds believers that، *“Let us not grow weary while doing good, for in due season we shall reap if we do not lose heart”* (Galatians 6:9)۔ Progress in faith often includes setbacks، questions، and failures, but disciple-makers are called to walk alongside others، providing encouragement and support at every stage۔ When progress seems slow, it is easy to lose heart، but disciple-makers trust that God is at work, even when the results are not immediately visible۔

column4: Being a disciple-maker requires a blend of spiritual dependence, commitment, and humility. It is a calling that demands patience and persistence while remaining Spirit-led and teachable. Disciple-makers are not expected to be perfect, but they must be faithful-abiding in Christ, investing in others, and trusting God to bring the growth and transformation in His timing. These qualities reflect Christ’s love and help others become mature disciples who, in turn, can disciple others.
column5: Being a disciple-maker requires a combination of spiritual dependence، commitment، and humility۔ It is a calling that demands patience and perseverance while remaining Spirit-led and teachable۔ Disciple-makers are not expected to be perfect، but they must be faithful-abiding in Christ، investing in others، and trusting God to bring growth and transformation in His time۔ These qualities reflect the love of Christ and help others become mature disciples who can, in turn, make disciples of others۔

column4: ## Practical Tools for Discipleship
column5: ## Practical Resources for Discipleship

column4: Effective discipleship requires intentional tools and practices that foster spiritual growth, accountability, and community. These tools help disciples develop a strong foundation in faith, grow in intimacy with God, and become equipped to disciple others. Practical methods such as Bible study, prayer, small groups, and mentorship provide both the structure and support needed for ongoing growth.
column5: Effective discipleship requires intentional resources and practices that foster spiritual growth، accountability، and community۔ These resources help disciples establish a strong foundation in faith، grow in closeness with God، and be equipped to make disciples of others۔ Practical methods, such as Bible study، prayer، small groups، and mentoring, provide the structure and support needed for ongoing progress۔

column4: ### Biblical Study
column5: ### Bible Study

column4: Engaging deeply with Scripture is the foundation of discipleship. Jesus emphasized the importance of God’s Word in spiritual growth, declaring that *“man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God”* (Matthew 4:4). Regular Bible study and memorization enable disciples to internalize truth, combat falsehoods, and apply God’s wisdom to daily life.
column5: Engaging deeply with Scripture is the foundation of discipleship۔ Jesus emphasized the importance of God’s word in spiritual growth, saying, *“Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God”* (Matthew 4:4)۔ Through regular Bible study and memorization, disciples internalize truth، resist lies، and apply God’s wisdom to everyday life۔

column4: Disciples must be encouraged to immerse themselves in Scripture, not merely as an academic exercise but to know God and transform their hearts (Psalms 119:105). Practical approaches, such as reading plans, study guides, and group discussions, provide opportunities to explore doctrine and discuss application in community. By building habits of regular study, disciples lay a solid foundation for spiritual maturity and fruitful ministry (2 Timothy 3:16-17).
column5: Disciples should be encouraged to immerse themselves in the Word, not merely as an academic exercise but to know God and see their hearts transformed (Psalm 119:105)۔ Practical methods such as reading plans، study guides، and group discussions provide opportunities to explore doctrines and discuss application together۔ By building regular study habits، disciples lay a strong foundation for spiritual maturity and fruitful ministry (2 Timothy 3:16-17)۔

column4: ### Prayer
column5: ### Prayer

column4: Prayer is the lifeline of discipleship, connecting believers to God’s presence, power, and guidance. Jesus taught His disciples how to pray in Luke 11:1-4, emphasizing both dependence on God and spiritual alignment with His will. Through prayer, disciples learn to seek God’s wisdom, intercede for others, and receive strength for ministry.
column5: Prayer is the lifeline of discipleship, connecting believers to God’s presence، power، and guidance۔ Jesus taught His disciples to pray in Luke 11:1-4، and emphasized both dependence on God and spiritual alignment with His will۔ Through prayer, disciples learn to seek God’s wisdom، intercede for others، and find strength for service۔

column4: Teaching disciples how to pray-both individually and corporately-equips them to cultivate intimacy with God and discern His leading (Philippians 4:6-7). Incorporating prayer journals, prayer groups, and fasting practices fosters spiritual discipline and empowerment, ensuring disciples remain Spirit-led and mission-focused.
column5: Teaching disciples how to pray-individually and corporately-equips them to grow in closeness with God and to discern His guidance (Philippians 4:6-7)۔ Incorporating prayer journals، prayer groups، and fasting practices fosters spiritual discipline and strength، and ensures that disciples remain Spirit-led and mission-focused۔

column4: ### Small Groups and Community
column5: ### Small Groups and Community

column4: Discipleship thrives in community. The early church modeled relational discipleship through fellowship, prayer, and breaking bread together (Acts 2:42-47). Small groups and accountability partnerships provide a safe space for disciples to grow together, share struggles, and celebrate victories.
column5: Discipleship thrives in community۔ The early church modeled relational discipleship through fellowship، prayer، and breaking bread together (Acts 2:42-47)۔ Small groups and accountability partnerships provide a safe environment where disciples can grow together، share struggles، and celebrate victories۔

column4: The local church serves as the central hub for discipleship relationships, offering opportunities for group Bible studies, prayer meetings, and fellowship events. These gatherings allow disciples to practice love, bear one another’s burdens (Galatians 6:2), and encourage one another toward spiritual maturity (Hebrews 10:24-25). Small groups also provide a framework for multiplying leaders, as mature disciples train and send others to lead groups and mentor new believers.
column5: The local church serves as the central hub for discipleship relationships، and provides opportunities for group Bible study، prayer meetings، and fellowship events۔ These gatherings give disciples the opportunity to practice love، to bear one another’s burdens (Galatians 6:2)، and to encourage one another toward spiritual maturity (Hebrews 10:24-25)۔ Small groups also provide a structure for developing leaders، as mature disciples train and send others to lead groups and mentor new believers۔

column4: ### Mentorship
column5: ### Mentoring

column4: Mentorship provides a personal and intentional approach to discipleship. Jesus modeled this by investing deeply in the twelve disciples, walking with them through teaching, correction, and encouragement. Similarly, one-on-one relationships allow disciple-makers to tailor guidance to individual needs, helping disciples develop in faith, character, and leadership.
column5: Mentoring provides a personal and intentional approach to discipleship۔ Jesus set the example by investing deeply in the twelve disciples، walking with them through teaching، correction، and encouragement۔ Likewise، one-on-one relationships allow disciple-makers to tailor guidance to individual needs، enabling disciples to grow in faith، character، and leadership۔

column4: Mentors serve as accountability partners, offering support, prayer, and wisdom during times of growth and struggle. Practical tools like spiritual assessments, goal-setting, and regular check-ins ensure that disciples stay focused and motivated. Peer relationships within mentorship structures also foster mutual growth, as both mentor and disciple learn from shared experiences (Proverbs 27:17).
column5: Mentors serve as accountability partners، and provide support، prayer، and wisdom during times of growth and struggle۔ Practical tools like spiritual assessments، goal setting، and regular check-ins help ensure that disciples remain focused and encouraged۔ Peer relationships within mentoring structures also promote mutual growth، as both mentor and disciple learn from shared experiences (Proverbs 27:17)۔
